Hello @jsumners!

Using `--before`, the certs are generated at the start of the test suite before the tests actually run.
And by moving `--before` inside the `.taprc`, -according to the documentation-, the script will be executed every time the “tap” command is used, which means: the script will also be executed when running a single test, e.g: `tap test/something.test.js`

Hi @mcollina!
To fix the linting error, we should undo the last commit.

> which means: the script will also be executed when running a single test, e.g: `tap test/something.test.js`

I addressed that. The before script _will not_ be run when invoking `node test/something.test.js`. Thus, this breaks the natural script nature of our tests and makes them wholly dependent on using a test runner.

issue_context.title: test: auto generate test certificate
issue_context.body:
## 🚀 Feature Proposal

Move the current static test certification to auto generate before the test start.
https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/main/test/https/fastify.cert
https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/main/test/https/fastify.key

## Motivation

It can reduce the `false-positive` warning from security scanner.
comments: How to go about this one?

@makuzaverite 
Read More: 
https://node-tap.org/docs/api/test-lifecycle-events/#tbeforefn
You can use the life-cycle of `tap` to generate the `keypair` before the test.

https://nodejs.org/api/crypto.html#crypto_crypto_generatekeypair_type_options_callback
Generate `keypair` by `crypto`.
FWIW, this is one of the simplest ways I've managed to create compatible certificates -- https://github.com/jsumners/self-cert
